title: Macular Degeneration Care in Pine Beach, NJ | Academy Vision
metaDescription: Macular degeneration affects the central vision you use to read and drive. With regular eye exams, Academy Vision in Pine Beach can detect early signs.
h1: Monitoring Macular Degeneration in Pine Beach
kicker: Protecting the Vision You Rely on Most
lede:
The macula is a small area at the center of the retina with a big job. It gives you the sharp, detailed vision you use to read, drive, thread a needle, and pick out a friend’s face across a room. Age-related macular degeneration, often called AMD, gradually wears that area down.

At Academy Vision, regular eye exams let us detect early signs and help you maintain your quality of life. We’ll keep an ongoing watch on your central vision and explain any change in plain language.

sections.heading: Early Macular Degeneration Is Easy to Miss
sections.html:
In its early stage, macular degeneration usually causes no symptoms. The first signs are often small yellow deposits under the retina called drusen, which an eye doctor can see during an exam well before your vision changes.

Most people have the dry form, which tends to progress slowly over years. A smaller group develops the wet form, where abnormal blood vessels grow beneath the retina and leak. Wet AMD can blur or distort central vision quickly, so prompt attention matters.

sections.heading: Three Reasons to Keep Up With Macular Checks
sections.html:
• A careful look at the macula. An exam can pick up changes you wouldn’t notice yet in daily life.
  • A baseline to compare against. Knowing how your macula looked last year makes new changes easier to recognize.
  • A clear plan. Whether the answer is routine checkups or a closer watch, you’ll understand what comes next.

Early detection and monitoring of macular degeneration is one of Dr. Tyler Lesko’s clinical specialties.

sections.heading: What the Check Involves, and What Comes Next
sections.html:
Checking for macular degeneration usually means testing how sharply you see, then taking a careful look at the macula itself. Some eye doctors also suggest a simple home check with a grid of straight lines, often called an Amsler grid, so you can notice wavy or missing areas between visits.

If early signs appear, the usual next step is closer monitoring and attention to the everyday habits that protect your eyes. If the wet form is suspected, a retina specialist should see you promptly, because treatment works best when it starts early. Either way, we’ll talk through what we find in plain language.

sections.heading: A Lasting Condition Deserves a Lasting Record
sections.html:
Macular degeneration is a long-term condition, and the most useful information is how it changes over time. Seeing the same practice each year keeps your history in one place, so every exam can be compared with the ones before it.

A quick vision screening, or a visit that only updates your glasses prescription, shows how clearly you see but isn’t meant to follow the health of your macula. Our comprehensive eye exams take a close look at your eye health, including any signs of concern. Families in and around Pine Beach have trusted us with their vision for over 40 years.

sections.heading: Part of Your Medical Eye Care
sections.html: Macular degeneration is one of the conditions we manage as part of our medical eye care. You may also want to read about eye exams for seniors, along with glaucoma monitoring and cataract care, since glaucoma and cataracts also become more common with age.

faq.a: There’s no cure yet, but there is real help. For the wet form, treatments given by retina specialists, usually injections into the eye, can slow vision loss and sometimes improve sight. For some people with intermediate or advanced AMD, a specific vitamin and mineral formula studied in large clinical trials, known as AREDS2, can lower the chance of it getting worse. Ask your eye doctor before starting any supplement.

faq.q: Will macular degeneration make me blind?
faq.a: AMD rarely causes total blindness, because side vision usually stays intact. As it advances, though, it can make reading, driving, and recognizing faces harder, which is why steady monitoring is worth it.

faq.q: How fast does it progress, and how often should it be checked?
faq.a: Dry AMD usually changes slowly, over years, while wet AMD can change within weeks. The right checkup interval comes down to how advanced your AMD is and to risk factors like age, family history, and smoking. If straight lines suddenly look wavy, or a dark or empty spot appears in the center of your vision, call us at (732) 978-9306 right away. Sudden vision loss needs emergency care immediately.

Not smoking is one of the most important steps you can take. A diet rich in leafy greens and fish, regular exercise, and keeping blood pressure and cholesterol in check also support the health of your retina.

cta.heading: Book a Macular Check in Pine Beach
cta.html: Whether you’ve noticed changes or simply want peace of mind, a careful look at your macula is a good place to start. Call us at (732) 978-9306 or book your visit online.
